Height ~76px · Rows 2 (top dense · sub thin) · Density very high · Scan time ~1.2s (requires familiarity) · Best for power users · trading-desk workflow · wide screens

✓ Pros

  • Most compact — only 76px of vertical real estate
  • All info one glance — no scrolling, no expanding
  • Familiar to pros — Bloomberg/CapIQ desk users adapt instantly
  • Best on ultrawide monitors — 1920px+ fits naturally
  • Conflict badge inline — never lost

✗ Cons

  • Hostile to newcomers — requires memorizing tile codes (V, S, ER, etc.)
  • Breaks on narrow screens — < 1400px will wrap awkwardly
  • No visual hierarchy — all chips look equal weight
  • Mobile-unfriendly — fundamentally a desktop-only design

Height ~180px · Rows 2 (hero / bottom) · Density balanced · visual · Scan time ~0.5s (eye locks on arc) · Best for mixed audience · sales demos · executive review

✓ Pros

  • Strongest visual identity — arc is unmistakable
  • Score visible from across the room — demo-friendly
  • Balanced hierarchy — primary (arc) → secondary (4 tiles) → tertiary (lenses)
  • No information loss vs current — all 8 lenses + 4 KPIs preserved
  • Works on narrow screens — grid collapses gracefully

✗ Cons

  • Tallest of the three at 180px
  • Arc takes "premium" center space — power users may want that for data
  • SVG arc adds render cost (negligible but real)
  • Aesthetics-forward — some quants find it gimmicky

Height ~160px · Layout 260px sticky-rail + content · Density balanced · Scan time ~0.7s · Best for users who scroll-and-reference · keeps verdict in view always

✓ Pros

  • Sticky verdict — DELL · BUY · T1 stays visible as you scroll sub-tabs
  • Verdict is huge and unmissable — full-width column block
  • Right column is flexible — could swap in any drill-down content per sub-tab
  • Strong visual anchor — left rail = "ticker identity" forever
  • Mode pills + lens row sit comfortably — no cramming

✗ Cons

  • Loses 260px horizontal — content area shrinks
  • Requires sticky scroll behavior — extra implementation
  • Tall on small screens — wraps awkwardly < 1100px
  • Eye-tracking pattern is left-right-down — less natural than top-down
  • Existing kairos tabs may need realignment — pixel-cost to refactor

My recommendation: Different layouts win for different workflows.
  • Choose A (3-zone) if your priority is a clean, balanced, familiar layout. Safe choice. Easy to ship.
  • Choose B (Trading Desk) if you/your users live on the page and want minimal scroll. Best on a 27"+ monitor.
  • Choose C (Cockpit) if visual identity matters — sales demos, screenshots, executive walkthroughs.
  • Choose D (Left Rail) if users spend long sessions in sub-tabs and you want the verdict always visible.
